title: A beautiful example
hook: in the messenger of Allah you have a beautiful example (33:21)
carry: do the hard thing with them

segments.voice: Yesterday: hidden joy, qurrat a'yun, kept hidden for those who prayed unseen. Your line was joy kept hidden.

Medina, under threat. A confederacy of tribes is marching on the city. On the advice of Salman the Persian, the biographies say, the Muslims decide to dig a trench across the open side of the city. Men with picks and baskets, in the cold, short on food, racing against time. And among them, carrying earth on his back until the dust covered his skin, the leader of the community. Surah Al-Ahzab, the Confederates, the thirty-third, tells of those days.

The surah describes the fear honestly. Eyes grew wild, hearts reached the throats, and people began to think all kinds of thoughts about God. Some slipped away with excuses. And right in the middle of that account comes the verse. Pickthall: "Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much." The Arabic is uswatun hasanah. Hasanah is good, beautiful, excellent. Uswah is a model, someone you copy. The verse isn't on a poster. It's in a trench. Bukhari reports that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ dug and carried earth alongside everyone, chanting verses with them as they worked. Jabir reported that when a huge rock blocked the digging, the Prophet came and broke it, and that he had a stone tied against his stomach from hunger, the same as the rest. The example wasn't in how he talked about hardship. It was in doing the hardship with them. That's what Muslims mean by following the sunnah, the Prophet's way: not only the prayers and fasts, but small things. Smiling, which a hadith calls charity. Helping at home, which 'A'isha said he did, serving his family. Greeting first. Eating with the right hand. The Qur'an uses uswah of Ibrahim, too. This week's lines, from Luqman to As-Sajdah, ran from Luqman's first advice and a mother's wahn, through a lowered voice and words that don't run out, to up in the night and joy kept hidden. And today: a beautiful example.
screen: `HEARTS REACHED THE THROATS.` · `USWATUN HASANAH.` · `CARRYING EARTH WITH THEM.` · `THE SUNNAH IN SMALL THINGS.`

segments.voice: Choose one small, everyday thing the Prophet is reported to have done: smiling at the next person you meet, helping with a chore unasked, saying salam first, sitting down to drink, eating with the right hand and saying bismillah. Pick just one, and picture the moment in your day where it fits. If you're not Muslim, you can still pick one as a kindness worth trying.
Uswah. A model to copy; uswatun hasanah, the beautiful example the Qur'an names in the Prophet, in the middle of the trench. Today's word.
Your line: do the hard thing with them. An example is shown, not told. That closes the week.

howItsDone: Muslims follow the sunnah, the Prophet's example, in worship and in daily habits, learning it from the hadith collections and from biographies of his life.

fork.reveal: Bukhari reports that the Prophet dug and carried earth with them, hungry like the rest; 33:21 calls him a beautiful example.

original.note: Arabic: a beautiful example; uswah is a model to copy, hasanah is good or beautiful.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Prophet was a good role model.
what it means: an example shown under siege, by doing the hardship alongside people, and copied by Muslims in small daily habits.
what a scholar hears: uswatun hasanah in 33:21, set in the Battle of the Trench; the same phrase used of Ibrahim at 60:4; and the digging reports in Bukhari 4099–4101.
recall: the wise father of Surah thirty-one

chat.says: What does 'a beautiful example' mean in that verse about the Prophet?
options: Someone to copy: in the trench, he dug and went hungry alongside everyone.
A stirring speech about hardship he gave to the frightened army.
That only his formal prayers and fasts are meant to be copied.
chat.meaning: Uswah is a model to copy. The verse sits in the trench story, where he carried earth and went hungry with everyone.

Medina.meaning: the Prophet's city, under threat in this story

Salman.meaning: Salman the Persian; the biographies credit him with the trench idea

uswatun hasanah.meaning: a beautiful example, a model worth copying

sunnah.meaning: the Prophet's way, followed in big and small things
